contract: Tally durable job flow: submit/5 appends a requested record and jobs outbox item to the per-queue submission stream through an ELZ-010-owned Submitter; the Relay creates the Run stream (accepted) and a unique Oban job; each worker execution classifies its start and results with Elzoo.JobRun and writes attempt and terminal records by ELZ-009 CAS; cancel/3 (also before relay) and status/2. Attempt count, absolute deadline and policy persist with the Run. Entry points refuse inside a transaction on the configured Repo.
limits: One exemplar: one Run per Work Item, one pure step; no workflow engine, DAG, saga, cron, distributed scheduler, lease or external Effect.

Schema evolution deferred: only schema_version 1 exists; other record versions are refused as damaged ({:cancel, :damaged}) and other job-args versions as {:cancel, :unsupported_version}; nothing is upcast; state/schema-evolution stays planned; the first format change must meet the ELZ-010 R6/R9 corpus requirements under a new task and follow the Piece-ID evolution rule; mixed-version rolling deploys are unsupported.
No exactly-once execution: a rescued live attempt may run concurrently and consumes Run budget; its results are fenced by CAS and attempt identity.

A stalled Run (non-terminal, provider job terminal or gone) is reported by status/2, never repaired, and its deadline is not recorded; deadlines use node clocks and are evaluated only when a worker runs.
Submits per queue are serialized through one Submitter and one CAS row; Submitter memory grows with distinct job keys; submission and Run streams are not retained.
The caller-transaction guard checks only the configured Repo; Store behaviour inside a caller transaction is ELZ-032's (#52).

A Store write blocked longer than the consumer's Lifeline rescue_after lets Oban rescue the live execution, consuming an Oban attempt; repeated blocked writes can exhaust the provider slack, discard the job and stall the Run. A Writer call that times out is reported as snooze/indeterminate; if its write still commits, the next execution begins a new Run attempt.

grounding.claim: Listed scenarios DJ1–DJ8, DJ10–DJ17, DJ19–DJ21 and DJ12b on Memory and a disposable PostgreSQL with Oban 2.24.2: success, duplicates, relay crash/lock/foreign items, retry, exhaustion, permanent failure, deadlines, cancellation incl. before relay, restart without budget reset, rescued stale attempts, duplicate jobs, lost commit reply, damaged/version refusal, unreachable store, stalled reporting, caller-transaction refusal, stale pre-start executions, relay page limits, slow Store writes past the call timeout, bound-job status and backoff indexing; finite scenarios, not proofs.
DJ9: SIGKILL of a separate OS process executing attempt 1; a new Oban instance's Lifeline rescue resumes at Run attempt 2 with counts not reset.
Local observation of the victim exit status 137 and record sequence in the test log; not a production claim.

Oban 2.24.2 job persistence, FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED claim, retry staging, unique insert (advisory lock plus query, not a constraint), snooze attempt handling, cancel_all_jobs and Lifeline time-based rescue (documented to rescue live jobs) are upstream contracts.
Jason 1.4.5 encoding/decoding of record payloads is an upstream contract.
Ecto SQL 3.14.0 Repo, transaction and in_transaction?/0 semantics are upstream contracts.
PostgreSQL transaction atomicity, row locking, advisory locks and READ COMMITTED behaviour reached through Postgrex 0.22.4 are upstream server contracts, not local proofs.
Elixir validation, exceptions, exit trapping and BEAM execution are upstream contracts, not proved here.
OTP 29.1.2 GenServer, Supervisor, Task.Supervisor, links/monitors and :persistent_term semantics are upstream contracts; no exactly-once or disk durability guarantee.

Handlers are pure and deterministic; node clocks have bounded skew; one Submitter and one Relay per queue per cluster by convention (CAS catches violations); production PostgreSQL uses fsync=on and synchronous_commit=on.

telemetry.contract: No events emitted; transitions are return values and Run records; Oban emits its own job events.

config.contract: Start-time queue, Store, Repo, Oban name, handler, clock, provider slack, snooze, relay limit/interval and writer_timeout_ms (default 35_000 = Store write timeout 30_000 + 5_000 margin) (fixed, no hot change); per-submit max_attempts, backoff and absolute deadline fixed for the Run's life.

control.contract: cancel/3 with the complete result set {:ok, :cancelled}, {:error, {:terminal, phase}}, {:error, :not_found}, {:error, {:invalid, :requested_by}}, {:error, :not_started} (no live Assembly registration for the queue on this node), {:error, :caller_transaction}, {:error, :damaged}, {:error, :unavailable} (nothing sent: Writer could not start, Submitter query failed, or the Assembly's Task.Supervisor did not exist), {:error, :contended}, {:error, {:rejected, reason}}, {:indeterminate, info} (a write may have been sent: Store indeterminate, a Writer call exit or timeout, a task start exit or the 5_000 ms start timeout, or the task's exit or result timeout), and read-only status/2. Lifecycle: a Registration process (first child) owns the queue's config and worker runner and erases both when it terminates; entry points and the runner also require the owner to be alive, so a stopped or killed Assembly gives {:error, :not_started} and its pending jobs snooze without running a handler; restarting the same queue re-registers. Submitter and Relay have OTP start/stop only (one_for_one); no pause/drain.
